quotes: “ The gentleman is n't in , ”
“ Oh , I divined it ! ”
“ So you have made up your mind to stay ? ”
“ Yes , ”
“ and I am wrong . One ought not to accustom oneself to impossible pleasures when there are a thousand demands upon one . ”
“ Oh , I can imagine ! ”
“ Ah ! no ; for you , you are a man ! ”
“ But pardon me ! ”
“ It is wrong of me . I weary you with my eternal complaints . ”
“ No , never , never ! ”
“ all that I had dreamed ! ”

“ And I ! Oh , I too have suffered ! Often I went out ; I went away . I dragged myself along the quays , seeking distraction amid the din of the crowd without being able to banish the heaviness that weighed upon me . In an engraver 's shop on the boulevard there is an Italian print of one of the Muses . She is draped in a tunic , and she is looking at the moon , with forget-me-nots in her flowing hair . Something drove me there continually ; I stayed there hours together . ”
“ She resembled you a little . ”
“ Often , ”
“ I wrote you letters that I tore up . ”

“ I sometimes fancied that some chance would bring you . I thought I recognised you at street-corners , and I ran after all the carriages through whose windows I saw a shawl fluttering , a veil like yours . ”

“ But the most wretched thing , is it not — is to drag out , as I do , a useless existence . If our pains were only of some use to someone , we should find consolation in the thought of the sacrifice . ”
“ I should much like , ”
“ to be a nurse at a hospital . ”
“ Alas ! men have none of these holy missions , and I see nowhere any calling — unless perhaps that of a doctor . ”
“ But why ? ”
“ Why ? ”
“ Because I loved you so ! ”
“ I always suspected it . ”
“ And our poor cactuses , where are they ? ”
“ The cold killed them this winter . ”

“ Ah ! how I have thought of them , do you know ? I often saw them again as of yore , when on the summer mornings the sun beat down upon your blinds , and I saw your two bare arms passing out amongst the flowers . ”
“ Poor friend ! ”
“ At that time you were to me I know not what incomprehensible force that took captive my life . Once , for instance , I went to see you ; but you , no doubt , do not remember it . ”
“ go on . ”

“ You were downstairs in the ante-room , ready to go out , standing on the last stair ; you were wearing a bonnet with small blue flowers ; and without any invitation from you , in spite of myself , I went with you . Every moment , however , I grew more and more conscious of my folly , and I went on walking by you , not daring to follow you completely , and unwilling to leave you . When you went into a shop , I waited in the street , and I watched you through the window taking off your gloves and counting the change on the counter . Then you rang at Madame Tuvache 's ; you were let in , and I stood like an idiot in front of the great heavy door that had closed after you . ”
“ Yes , it is true — true — true ! ”
“ Well ! ”
“ Well ! ”
“ How is it that no one until now has ever expressed such sentiments to me ? ”
“ I have sometimes thought of it , ”
“ What a dream ! ”
“ And who prevents us from beginning now ? ”
“ I am too old ; you are too young . Forget me ! Others will love you ; you will love them . ”
“ Not as you ! ”
“ What a child you are ! Come , let us be sensible . I wish it . ”
“ Ah ! forgive me ! ”
“ Ah ! how late it is ! ”
“ how we do chatter ! ”
“ It has even made me forget the theatre . And poor Bovary has left me here especially for that . Monsieur Lormeaux , of the Rue Grand-Pont , was to take me and his wife . ”
“ Really ! ”
“ Yes . ”
“ Ah ! you can jest . Enough ! enough ! Oh , for pity 's sake , let me see you once — only once ! ”
“ Oh , not here ! ”
“ Where you will . ”
“ To-morrow at eleven o'clock in the cathedral . ”
“ You are mad ! Ah ! you are mad ! ”
“ Tomorrow ! ”
“ I 'll give it to him myself , ”
“ he will come . ”
“ It is still too early , ”
“ The gentleman , no doubt , does not belong to these parts ? The gentleman would like to see the curiosities of the church ? ”
“ No ! ”
“ Read ! ”
“ Oh , no ! ”
“ Madame , no doubt , does not belong to these parts ? Madame would like to see the curiosities of the church ? ”
“ Oh , no ! ”
“ Why not ? ”
“ This simple stone covers Pierre de Breze , lord of Varenne and of Brissac , grand marshal of Poitou , and governor of Normandy , who died at the battle of Montlhery on the 16th of July , 1465 . ”

“ And on the right , this gentleman all encased in iron , on the prancing horse , is his grandson , Louis de Breze , lord of Breval and of Montchauvet , Count de Maulevrier , Baron de Mauny , chamberlain to the king , Knight of the Order , and also governor of Normandy ; died on the 23rd of July , 1531 — a Sunday , as the inscription specifies ; and below , this figure , about to descend into the tomb , portrays the same person . It is not possible , is it , to see a more perfect representation of annihilation ? ”

“ Near him , this kneeling woman who weeps is his spouse , Diane de Poitiers , Countess de Breze , Duchess de Valentinois , born in 1499 , died in 1566 , and to the left , the one with the child is the Holy Virgin . Now turn to this side ; here are the tombs of the Ambroise . They were both cardinals and archbishops of Rouen . That one was minister under Louis XII . He did a great deal for the cathedral . In his will he left thirty thousand gold crowns for the poor . ”
“ Truly , ”

“ it adorned the tomb of Richard Coeur de Lion , King of England and Duke of Normandy . It was the Calvinists , sir , who reduced it to this condition . They had buried it for spite in the earth , under the episcopal seat of Monsignor . See ! this is the door by which Monsignor passes to his house . Let us pass on quickly to see the gargoyle windows . ”
“ Sir ! sir ! The steeple ! the steeple ! ”
“ No , thank you ! ”
“ But where are we going ? ”
“ Sir ! ”
“ What is it ? ”
“ Idiot ! ”
“ Go and get me a cab ! ”
“ Ah ! Leon ! Really — I do n't know — if I ought , ”
“ It is done at Paris . ”
“ At all events , go out by the north porch , ”
“ so as to see the Resurrection , the Last Judgment , Paradise , King David , and the Condemned in Hell-flames . ”
“ Where to , sir ? ”
“ Where you like , ”
“ Go on , ”
“ No , straight on ! ”
“ Get on , will you ? ”
“ Madame , you must go at once to Monsieur Homais . It 's for something important . ”
“ Who told you to go and fetch it in the Capharnaum . ”
“ What is it ? What is the matter ? ”
“ What is it ? ”

“ We are making preserves ; they are simmering ; but they were about to boil over , because there is too much juice , and I ordered another pan . Then he , from indolence , from laziness , went and took , hanging on its nail in my laboratory , the key of the Capharnaum . ”
“ Presently ! Do you know to what you exposed yourself ? Did n't you see anything in the corner , on the left , on the third shelf ? Speak , answer , articulate something . ”

“ Ah ! you do n't know ! Well , then , I do know ! You saw a bottle of blue glass , sealed with yellow wax , that contains a white powder , on which I have even written ‘ Dangerous ! ’ And do you know what is in it ? Arsenic ! And you go and touch it ! You take a pan that was next to it ! ”
“ Next to it ! ”
“ Arsenic ! You might have poisoned us all . ”
“ Or poison a patient ! ”

“ Do you want to see me in the prisoner 's dock with criminals , in a court of justice ? To see me dragged to the scaffold ? Do n't you know what care I take in managing things , although I am so thoroughly used to it ? Often I am horrified myself when I think of my responsibility ; for the Government persecutes us , and the absurd legislation that rules us is a veritable Damocles ’ sword over our heads . ”

“ That is your return for all the kindness we have shown you ! That is how you recompense me for the really paternal care that I lavish on you ! For without me where would you be ? What would you be doing ? Who provides you with food , education , clothes , and all the means of figuring one day with honour in the ranks of society ? But you must pull hard at the oar if you 're to do that , and get , as , people say , callosities upon your hands . Fabricando fit faber , age quod agis . ”

“ I am beginning to repent terribly of having taken you up ! I should certainly have done better to have left you to rot in your poverty and the dirt in which you were born . Oh , you 'll never be fit for anything but to herd animals with horns ! You have no aptitude for science ! You hardly know how to stick on a label ! And there you are , dwelling with me snug as a parson , living in clover , taking your ease ! ”
“ how am I to tell you ? It is a misfortune ! ”
“ Empty it ! Clean it ! Take it back ! Be quick ! ”
“ CONJUGAL — LOVE ! ”
“ Ah ! very good ! very good ! very pretty ! And illustrations ! Oh , this is too much ! ”
“ No , do not touch it ! ”
“ Leave the room , ”

“ It is not that I entirely disapprove of the work . Its author was a doctor ! There are certain scientific points in it that it is not ill a man should know , and I would even venture to say that a man must know . But later — later ! At any rate , not till you are man yourself and your temperament is formed . ”
“ Ah ! my dear ! ”
“ Yes , I know , I know ! ”
“ I should have liked to see him again ! ”
“ How old was your father ? ”
“ Fifty-eight . ”
“ Ah ! ”
“ My poor mother ! what will become of her now ? ”
“ Did you enjoy yourself yesterday ? ”
“ Yes . ”
“ He does n't even remember any more about it , ”
“ Hallo ! you 've a pretty bouquet , ”
“ Yes , ”
“ it 's a bouquet I bought just now from a beggar . ”
“ I beg your pardon , ”
“ but I should like to have a private talk with you . ”
“ It 's about that affair — you know . ”
“ Oh , yes ! certainly . ”
“ Could n't you , my darling ? ”
“ It is nothing particular . No doubt , some household trifle . ”
“ And so you 're quite well again ? ”
“ Ma foi ! I saw your husband in a sad state . He 's a good fellow , though we did have a little misunderstanding . ”
“ Why , you know well enough , ”
“ It was about your little fancies — the travelling trunks . ”
“ We made it up , all the same , and I 've come again to propose another arrangement . ”

“ And he would do better to give it over to someone else — to you , for example . With a power of attorney it could be easily managed , and then we ( you and I ) would have our little business transactions together . ”
“ The one you 've on is good enough for the house , but you want another for calls . I saw that the very moment that I came in . I 've the eye of an American ! ”
“ Monsieur Guillaumin ”
“ I do n't trust him overmuch . Notaries have such a bad reputation . Perhaps we ought to consult — we only know — no one . ”
“ No , I will go ! ”
“ How good you are ! ”

“ Perhaps it belongs to the party I took out the other day . A lot of jolly folk , gentlemen and ladies , with cakes , champagne , cornets — everything in style ! There was one especially , a tall handsome man with small moustaches , who was that funny ! And they all kept saying , ‘ Now tell us something , Adolphe — Dolpe , ’ I think . ”
“ You are in pain ? ”
“ Oh , it 's nothing ! No doubt , it is only the night air . ”
“ So you can assure me it is all right ? ”
“ Yes , certainly . ”
“ is she so very anxious to get this power of attorney ? ”
“ I would rather die ! ”
“ Adieu ! adieu ! When shall I see you again ? ”
“ Bravo ! very goodl You are wrong to stop . Go on ! ”
“ Oh , no ; it is execrable ! My fingers are quite rusty . ”
“ Very well ; to please you ! ”
“ Twenty francs a lesson , that 's too dear ! ”
“ But it seems to me that one might be able to do it for less ; for there are artists of no reputation , and who are often better than the celebrities . ”
“ Find them ! ”

“ How obstinate you are sometimes ! I went to Barfucheres to-day . Well , Madame Liegard assured me that her three young ladies who are at La Misericorde have lessons at fifty sous apiece , and that from an excellent mistress ! ”
“ Ah ! my poor piano ! ”
“ What a pity ! she had so much talent ! ”

“ You are wrong . One should never let any of the faculties of nature lie fallow . Besides , just think , my good friend , that by inducing madame to study ; you are economising on the subsequent musical education of your child . For my own part , I think that mothers ought themselves to instruct their children . That is an idea of Rousseau 's , still rather new perhaps , but that will end by triumphing , I am certain of it , like mothers nursing their own children and vaccination . ”
“ If you liked , ”
“ a lesson from time to time , that would n't after all be very ruinous . ”
“ are only of use when followed up . ”
“ Oh , do not move ! do not speak ! look at me ! Something so sweet comes from your eyes that helps me so much ! ”
“ Child , do you love me ? ”
“ Till Thursday , till Thursday . ”
“ Adieu ! ”
“ No , ”
“ But , ”
“ you seem so strange this evening . ”
“ Oh , it 's nothing ! nothing ! ”
“ Come ! ”
“ that will do . Now you can go . ”
“ Ah ! you too , you will leave me ! You will marry ! You will be like all the others . ”
“ What others ? ”
“ You are all evil ! ”
“ Not like you , ”
“ He was a ship 's captain , my dear . ”
“ Ah ! how happy we should be there ! ”
“ Are we not happy ? ”
“ Yes , that is true , ”
“ I am mad . Kiss me ! ”
“ It is Mademoiselle Lempereur , is n't it , who gives you lessons ? ”
“ Yes . ”
“ at Madame Liegeard 's . I spoke to her about you , and she does n't know you . ”
“ Ah ! no doubt she forgot my name . ”
“ there are several Demoiselles Lempereur at Rouen who are music-mistresses . ”
“ Possibly ! ”
“ But I have my receipts here . See ! ”
“ Oh , I will find them , ”
“ Received , for three months ’ lessons and several pieces of music , the sum of sixty-three francs .— Felicie Lempereur , professor of music . ”
“ How the devil did it get into my boots ? ”
“ have fallen from the old box of bills that is on the edge of the shelf . ”
“ I must have some money . ”
“ But if you have n't any ready money , you have an estate . ”
“ If I were in your place , ”
“ I should clear myself of my debts , and have money left over . ”
“ Have n't you your power of attorney ? ”
“ Leave me the bill , ”
“ Oh , it is n't worth while , ”
“ Never mind the price ! ”
“ Frankly , ”
“ that 's a good price . ”
“ It really grieves me , on my word ! to see you depriving yourself all at once of such a big sum as that . ”
“ What ! what ! ”
“ Oh ! ”
“ one puts anything one likes on receipts . Do n't you think I know what household affairs are ? ”
“ Sign these , ”
“ and keep it all ! ”
“ But if I give you the surplus , ”
“ is that not helping you ? ”
“ Received of Madame Bovary four thousand francs . ”
“ Now who can trouble you , since in six months you 'll draw the arrears for your cottage , and I do n't make the last bill due till after you 've been paid ? ”
“ You understand — in business — sometimes . And with the date , if you please , with the date . ”
“ Really , you must confess , considering the quantity , it is n't too dear . ”
“ but she wants to see the account . ”

“ Could n't you do without a carpet ? Why have recovered the arm-chairs ? In my time there was a single arm-chair in a house , for elderly persons — at any rate it was so at my mother 's , who was a good woman , I can tell you . Everybody can n't be rich ! No fortune can hold out against waste ! I should be ashamed to coddle myself as you do ! And yet I am old . I need looking after . And there ! there ! fitting up gowns ! fallals ! What ! silk for lining at two francs , when you can get jaconet for ten sous , or even for eight , that would do well enough ! ”
“ Ah ! Madame , enough ! enough ! ”
“ What ? ”
“ Thank you , ”
“ Oh , my God ! ”
“ Ah ! you really are wrong ! You come here and make scenes with her ! ”

“ No , no ! You love her better than me , and you are right . It is natural . For the rest , so much the worse ! You will see . Good day — for I am not likely to come soon again , as you say , to make scenes . ”
“ I understand , ”
“ a man of science can n't be worried with the practical details of life . ”
“ I am mad , ”
“ no doubt they kept her to dinner at Monsieur Lormeaux ’ . ”
“ She probably stayed to look after Madame Dubreuil . Why , Madame Dubreuil has been dead these ten months ! Where can she be ? ”
“ What kept you yesterday ? ”
“ I was not well . ”
“ What was it ? Where ? How ? ”
“ At Mademoiselle Lempereur 's . ”
“ I was sure of it ! I was going there . ”
“ She went out just now ; but for the future do n't worry . I do not feel free , you see , if I know that the least delay upsets you like this . ”
“ Pshaw ! come along , ”
“ With pleasure ! ”
“ besides , I must invigorate my mind , for I am getting rusty here . We 'll go to the theatre , to the restaurant ; we 'll make a night of it . ”
“ Oh , my dear ! ”

“ Well , what ? Do you think I 'm not sufficiently ruining my health living here amid the continual emanations of the pharmacy ? But there ! that is the way with women ! They are jealous of science , and then are opposed to our taking the most legitimate distractions . No matter ! Count upon me . One of these days I shall turn up at Rouen , and we 'll go the pace together . ”
“ You must be very lonely , ”
“ here at Rouen . To be sure your lady-love does n't live far away . ”
“ The servant ! ”
“ I approve of that , ”
“ they have more passion . ”
“ And negresses ? ”
“ They are an artistic taste ! ”
“ Waiter ! two cups of coffee ! ”
“ Are we going ? ”
“ Ja ! ”
“ Ah ! I will escort you , ”
“ You will come back ? ”
“ Yes . ”
“ But when ? ”
“ Immediately . ”
“ I wanted to interrupt this visit , that seemed to me to annoy you . Let 's go and have a glass of garus at Bridoux ’ . ”
“ Leave Cujas and Barthole alone a bit . Who the devil prevents you ? Be a man ! Let 's go to Bridoux ’ . You 'll see his dog . It 's very interesting . ”
“ Let 's go to Bridoux ’ . It 's just by here , in the Rue Malpalu . ”
“ Presently ! I 'm coming ! We 'll go to the ‘ Fanal de Rouen ’ to see the fellows there . I 'll introduce you to Thornassin . ”
“ Do n't see them ; do n't go out ; think only of ourselves ; love me ! ”
“ Bah ! so much the worse . Let him deceive me ! What does it matter to me ? As If I cared for him ! ”
“ Yet I love him , ”
“ What answer am I to take Monsieur Vincart ? ”
“ tell him that I have n't it . I will send next week ; he must wait ; yes , till next week . ”
“ Your obedient ! ”
“ I am at your service . ”
“ What news ? ”
“ See ! ”
“ Well how can I help it ? ”
“ But I was pressed myself ; the knife was at my own throat . ”
“ And what will happen now ? ”
“ Oh , it 's very simple ; a judgment and then a distraint — that 's about it ! ”
“ I dare say ! Quiet Vincart ! You do n't know him ; he 's more ferocious than an Arab ! ”
“ Well , listen . It seems to me so far I 've been very good to you . ”

“ Not to speak of the bills signed by Monsieur Bovary , one for seven hundred francs , and another for three hundred . As to your little installments , with the interest , why , there 's no end to ‘ em ; one gets quite muddled over ‘ em . I 'll have nothing more to do with it . ”
“ And we agree , you say ? ”
“ Oh ! to anything you like . ”
“ Provided that Vincart will listen to me ! However , it 's settled . I do n't play the fool ; I 'm straight enough . ”

“ When I think that there 's a dress at threepence-halfpenny a yard , and warranted fast colours ! And yet they actually swallow it ! Of course you understand one does n't tell them what it really is ! ”
“ Is n't it lovely ? ”
“ It is very much used now for the backs of arm-chairs . It 's quite the rage . ”
“ Do not mention this to my husband ; you know how proud he is . Excuse me . Yours obediently . ”
“ Ah , no ! ”
“ I should worry her . ”
“ Call the servant , ”
“ You know , dearie , that mamma does not like to be disturbed . ”
“ Oh , go away ! ”
“ In virtue of the seizure in execution of a judgment . ”
“ By order of the king , law , and justice , to Madame Bovary . ”
“ To pay the sum of eight thousand francs . ”
“ She will be constrained thereto by every form of law , and notably by a writ of distraint on her furniture and effects . ”
“ You know what has happened to me ? No doubt it 's a joke ! ”
“ How so ? ”
“ My good lady , did you think I should go on to all eternity being your purveyor and banker , for the love of God ? Now be just . I must get back what I 've laid out . Now be just . ”
“ Ah ! so much the worse . The court has admitted it . There 's a judgment . It 's been notified to you . Besides , it is n't my fault . It 's Vincart 's . ”
“ Could you not — ? ”
“ Oh , nothing whatever . ”
“ But still , now talk it over . ”
“ Whose fault is that ? ”
“ While I 'm slaving like a nigger , you go gallivanting about . ”
“ Ah ! no lecturing . ”
“ There , that 'll do ! Anyone 'd think you wanted to seduce me ! ”
“ You are a wretch ! ”
“ Oh , oh ! go it ! go it ! ”
“ I will show you up . I shall tell my husband . ”
“ All right ! I too . I 'll show your husband something . ”
“ Do you think , ”
“ that he 'll not understand your little theft , the poor dear man ? ”
“ Ah ! I 'll show him ! I 'll show him ! ”
“ Bah ! when one has friends like you ! ”
“ I promise you , ”
“ I will sell something . ”
“ Get along ! ”
“ you 've not got anything . ”
“ Annette , do n't forget the three coupons of No . 14 . ”
“ It is too late . ”
“ But if I brought you several thousand francs — a quarter of the sum — a third — perhaps the whole ? ”
“ No ; it 's no use ! ”
“ I implore you , Monsieur Lheureux , just a few days more ! ”
“ There ! tears now ! ”
“ You are driving me to despair ! ”
“ What do I care ? ”
“ Allow me , madame . You allow me ? ”
“ Charming ! very pretty . ”
“ Ah ! a correspondence , ”
“ But allow me , for I must make sure the box contains nothing else . ”
“ Is anyone walking upstairs ? ”
“ No , ”
“ it is a window that has been left open , and is rattling in the wind . ”
“ What brings you here ? ”
“ Do I disturb you ? ”
“ I must speak to you , ”
“ No , no ! Down there , in our home ! ”
“ Leon , you will do me a service ? ”
“ Listen , I want eight thousand francs . ”
“ But you are mad ! ”
“ Not yet . ”
“ How on earth can I ? ”
“ What a coward you are ! ”
“ You are exaggerating the difficulty . Perhaps , with a thousand crowns or so the fellow could be stopped . ”
“ Go , try , try ! I will love you so ! ”
“ I have been to three people with no success . ”
“ If I were in your place I should soon get some . ”
“ But where ? ”
“ At your office . ”
“ However , if you do n't see me by three o'clock do not wait for me , my darling . I must be off now ; forgive me ! Goodbye ! ”
“ Take care ! ”
“ Charmed to see you , ”

“ I can n't understand why the authorities tolerate such culpable industries . Such unfortunates should be locked up and forced to work . Progress , my word ! creeps at a snail 's pace . We are floundering about in mere barbarism . ”
“ This , ”
“ is a scrofulous affection . ”
“ My friend , have you long had this terrible infirmity ? Instead of getting drunk at the public , you 'd do better to die yourself . ”
“ Now there 's a sou ; give me back two lairds , and do n't forget my advice : you 'll be the better for it . ”
“ Monsieur Homais , near the market , pretty well known . ”
“ for all this trouble you 'll give us your performance . ”
“ No farinaceous or milk food , wear wool next the skin , and expose the diseased parts to the smoke of juniper berries . ”
“ Come what may come ! ”
“ And then , who knows ? Why , at any moment could not some extraordinary event occur ? Lheureux even might die ! ”
“ Madame ! madame ! ”
“ it 's abominable ! ”
“ If I were you , madame , I should go to Monsieur Guillaumin . ”
“ You who know the house through the servant , has the master spoken sometimes of me ? ”
“ Yes , you 'd do well to go there . ”
“ Now this , ”
“ is the dining-room I ought to have . ”
“ I have come , ”
“ Do get closer to the stove ; put your feet up against the porcelain . ”
“ Beautiful things spoil nothing . ”
“ How was it , ”
“ that you did n't come to me ? ”
“ Why , hey ? Did I frighten you so much ? It is I , on the contrary , who ought to complain . We hardly know one another ; yet I am very devoted to you . You do not doubt that , I hope ? ”
“ Sir , I am waiting . ”
“ For what ? ”
“ This money . ”
“ Well , yes ! ”
“ For pity 's sake , stay . I love you ! ”
“ You are taking a shameless advantage of my distress , sir ! I am to be pitied — not to be sold . ”
“ What a wretch ! what a scoundrel ! what an infamy ! ”
“ Well ? ”
“ No ! ”
“ Impossible ! they will not ! ”
“ And the master 'll soon be in . ”
“ I know that well enough . Leave me alone . ”
“ Go away ! This carpet on which you are walking is no longer ours . In your own house you do not possess a chair , a pin , a straw , and it is I , poor man , who have ruined you . ”
“ Yes , ”
“ he will forgive me , he who would give a million if I would forgive him for having known me ! Never ! never ! ”
“ Ah ! there she is ! ”
“ She is begging him to give her time for paying her taxes . ”
“ Apparently ! ”
“ Do you think she wants to order something of him ? ”
“ Why , he does n't sell anything , ”
“ Is she making him advances ? ”
“ Oh , it 's too much ! ”
“ Madame ! what do you mean ? ”
“ But where is she ? ”
“ Nurse Rollet , ”
“ I am choking ; unlace me ! ”
“ Oh , leave off ! ”
“ What 's bothering her ? ”
“ Why has she come here ? ”
“ What time is it ? ”
“ Nearly three . ”
“ Ahl thanks , thanks ! ”
“ Be quick ! ”
“ But , my dear lady , I 'm going , I 'm going ! ”
“ There is no one at your house ! ”
“ What ? ”
“ Oh , no one ! And the doctor is crying . He is calling for you ; they 're looking for you . ”
“ What am I going to say ? How shall I begin ? ”
“ What ! it is you ! ”
“ Yes , it is I , Rodolphe . I should like to ask your advice . ”
“ You have not changed ; you are charming as ever ! ”
“ they are poor charms since you disdained them . ”
“ No matter ! ”
“ I have suffered much . ”
“ Such is life ! ”
“ been good to you at least , since our separation ? ”
“ Oh , neither good nor bad . ”
“ Perhaps it would have been better never to have parted . ”
“ Yes , perhaps . ”
“ You think so ? ”
“ Oh , Rodolphe ! if you but knew ! I loved you so ! ”

“ How did you think I could live without you ? One cannot lose the habit of happiness . I was desolate . I thought I should die . I will tell you about all that and you will see . And you — you fled from me ! ”

“ You love others , confess it ! Oh , I understand them , dear ! I excuse them . You probably seduced them as you seduced me . You are indeed a man ; you have everything to make one love you . But we 'll begin again , wo n't we ? We will love one another . See ! I am laughing ; I am happy ! Oh , speak ! ”
“ Why , you have been crying ! What for ? ”
“ Oh , forgive me ! You are the only one who pleases me . I was imbecile and cruel . I love you . I will love you always . What is it . Tell me ! ”
“ Well , I am ruined , Rodolphe ! You must lend me three thousand francs . ”
“ You know , ”

“ that my husband had placed his whole fortune at a notary 's . He ran away . So we borrowed ; the patients do n't pay us . Moreover , the settling of the estate is not yet done ; we shall have the money later on . But to-day , for want of three thousand francs , we are to be sold up .
